_meta.indication: NUZYRA is a tetracycline class antibacterial indicated for adults with community-acquired bacterial pneumonia (CABP) and acute bacterial skin and skin structure infections (ABSSSI) caused by susceptible microorganisms

pivotal_trials.nct: Not stated in the reviewed documents
pivotal_trials.design: Phase 3, randomized (1:1), double-blind, active comparator-controlled trial comparing omadacycline and moxifloxacin
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with community-acquired bacterial pneumonia (PORT Risk Class II, III, or IV)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Clinical success at the early clinical response (ECR) timepoint, assessed 72 to 120 hours after the first dose, in the ITT population; non-inferiority margin 10%
pivotal_trials.result: Clinical success rates similar in both groups (81.1% omadacycline, 82.7% moxifloxacin; treatment difference 95% CI -1.6 [-7.1, 3.8]); non-inferior to moxifloxacin

pivotal_trials.nct: Not stated in the reviewed documents
pivotal_trials.design: Phase 3, randomized (1:1), double-blind, active comparator-controlled, multi-center study comparing omadacycline (OMC) and linezolid (LZD), with IV-to-oral switch
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with acute bacterial skin and skin structure infections (ABSSSI)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Clinical success at early clinical response (ECR), 48 to 72 hours after first dose, in the mITT population (defined as ≥20% reduction in lesion size); 10% non-inferiority margin
pivotal_trials.result: Clinical success 84.8% omadacycline vs 85.5% linezolid; treatment difference -0.7 (95% CI -6.3, 4.9); non-inferior to linezolid

pivotal_trials.nct: Not stated in the reviewed documents
pivotal_trials.design: Phase 3, randomized, double-blind, double-dummy, comparator-controlled multicenter study (oral-only regimen: 450 mg PO loading then 300 mg PO)
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with acute bacterial skin and skin structure infections (ABSSSI); conducted in the US only
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Clinical success at ECR, 48 to 72 hours after first dose, in the mITT population; 10% non-inferiority margin
pivotal_trials.result: Clinical success 87.5% omadacycline vs 82.5% linezolid; treatment difference 5 (95% CI -0.2, 10.3); non-inferior to linezolid

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥2%) include nausea, vomiting, infusion site reactions, transaminase elevations, hypertension, headache, diarrhea, insomnia, and constipation. In the ABSSSI trials nausea occurred in 21.9% (vs 8.7% linezolid) and vomiting in 11.4% (vs 3.9%). The key serious safety concern was a mortality imbalance in the CABP trial (2% NUZYRA vs 1% moxifloxacin).
target_moa: Omadacycline is a tetracycline-class (aminomethylcycline) antibacterial that binds the 30S subunit of the bacterial ribosome, inhibiting binding of aminoacyl-tRNA and blocking bacterial protein synthesis; it retains activity in the presence of tetracycline efflux and ribosomal protection (Tet(O)) mechanisms

advisory_committee.vote: AMDAC met August 8, 2018: for ABSSSI 17 voted yes, 1 no; for CABP 14 voted yes, 4 no

summary.text: NUZYRA (omadacycline) was designated a Qualified Infectious Disease Product (QIDP) and received Fast Track Designation for CABP, ABSSSI and cUTI, and as such received priority review; it was approved on a full (traditional) basis at first cycle on October 02, 2018 following an August 8, 2018 AMDAC meeting, with no accelerated approval and no prior complete response letter.
